name: Kerr parametric oscillator at thermal occupation 0.6
question: How does a thermal bath change the probability of the favoured state of a swept Kerr parametric oscillator with a bias?
assumptions: Frame rotating at half the pump frequency; hbar = 1; rates in units of the single-photon loss kappa.
Loss and thermal excitation at occupation 0.6: the seed noise is (2 nbar + 1) times the vacuum noise.
Same Kerr coefficient, sweep and bias as the 27-photon oscillator: the control changes only the bath.
The law predicts a lower probability than at zero temperature, with the argument of the normal distribution function reduced by (2 nbar + 1)^(-1/2).

provenance.reference: thermal noise in parametrically driven oscillators, M. I. Dykman, Fluctuating Nonlinear Oscillators (Oxford, 2012), chapter 7
